title: Kalaignar Karunanidhi on the Verdict of History: 'Paper Flowers Carry No Fragrance'
summary: Reflecting upon decades of political turmoil, DMK leader M. Karunanidhi offered his famous literary aphorism: artificial propaganda may dazzle, but only genuine service endures in the living verdict of history.
full_text:
In the early 1980s, during a prolonged period of political adversity in the opposition, DMK cadres gathered at the party headquarters in Chennai, deeply demoralized by a relentless barrage of hostile media propaganda and malicious allegations.

A delegation of young district organizers approached party president M. Karunanidhi:
"Thalaivar! Our political adversaries flood the daily press with fabricated slanders, deliberately erasing our record of social justice and agrarian reforms. How can truth survive when lies are shouted through megaphones every day?"

Karunanidhi laid down his pen, adjusted his dark spectacles, and addressed the young workers with the serene composure of a veteran navigator who had weathered a hundred storms:

"My beloved brethren! Never permit transient slander to disturb your inner peace. Let me share a simple truth drawn from nature:
One can fashion artificial flowers out of brightly painted paper. Displayed in an ornate glass parlor, they may dazzle a passing stranger and seem even more flawless than real blossoms. But paper flowers carry no natural fragrance! The moment moisture touches them, the dye runs and the illusion dissolves.
A real rose, by contrast, blooms amidst sharp thorns; yet its sweet scent is a gift of nature that lingers in the morning air!

So it is with statecraft and history. Temporary power and propaganda can fabricate paper achievements, but they possess no moral fragrance. The genuine reforms we etched into the lives of millions—free bus passes for rural students, land titles for hut-dwellers, equal rights for backward communities—are living seeds planted in the soul of the people. Slander will be swept away like dust, but the verdict of history will honor the living truth!"

Karunanidhi’s lyrical metaphor revitalized the movement, affirming that principled service outlasts all artificial propaganda.
